newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco declares emergency due to storms.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco declares emergency due to storms.

text.p: San Francisco's mayor declared a state of local emergency due to storm damages of nearly $3.5 million, a spokesman said Friday.
Mayor Willie Brown's proclamation will be forwarded to Gov. Pete Wilson with the request that San Francisco be added to the state's declaration of emergency.
Brown's office said more than $2 million would be needed for repairs at the Hetch Hetchy water reservoir. City streets and sewer lines were also damaged in recent storms.
The city's office of emergency services said damage estimates could rise as further assessments are completed.
Inclusion in the state's emergency declaration would allow San Francisco residents to apply for federal assistance and low-interest disaster loans.
In addition, the city would become eligible for up to 75 percent reimbursement of approved costs and for hazard mitigation grants, Brown said.
The San Francisco Board of Supervisors must still ratify the proclamation.
Flooding caused by days of torrential rain and melting snow killed at least six people in California and flooded tens of thousands of acres of farmland and thousands of homes.

Early damage estimates have already passed $1.5 billion, and that included less than half of the 42 counties where Wilson has declared a state of emergency. The flood is almost certain to overtake 1995 floods as the most costly in state history, officials said.
